summary: In Greek mythology, Echemmon (Ancient Greek: Ἐχέμμων) was a Trojan prince, son of King Priam, whom Diomedes thrust from his chariot together with his brother Chromius — listed among Priam's sons in Apollodorus.

sections.heading: Son of Priam
paragraphs: Homer recounts that Diomedes took two sons of Priam, Echemmon and Chromius, the twain being in one car; even as a lion leaps among the kine, so he thrust both from their chariot against their will. Apollodorus likewise counts Echemmon among Priam's many sons. A later tradition (Dictys) instead pairs him with Aretus as victims of Odysseus.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: This atlas entry (echemmon-priamid) is Priam's son slain with Chromius by Diomedes. Distinct from Echemmon, a friend of Thoas whom Eurypylus of Mysia killed in Quintus of Smyrna's Fall of Troy.
